deferred.reason: UMD Extension heat-pump page states COP only as prose ratio (COP 3.0 means three units of heat per unit of electricity; 2-4x band) with no symbolic equation, units, or seasonal weighting; DOE FEMP water-heater page reports UEF compliance numbers (3.93/3.3/0.95) defined by 10 CFR 430 App. E without reproducing a scalar equation. Neither supports an independent seasonal delivered-heat/electricity equation, so no duplicate_of heat-to-electricity is submitted.

deferred.reason: OpenStax UP2 section 1.6 quotes insulating R factor as d/k in US units ft2-F-h/Btu with example values R-11/R-19. A US-customary R-value model is left out to keep this batch in coherent SI; a future batch can curate it with explicit unit conversion.

deferred.reason: UEF is computed by a multi-step regulatory recipe (draw pattern, standby loss, first-hour rating per 10 CFR 430 Subpart B Appendix E), not a single scalar equation expressible in the bounded grammar; excluded rather than fabricated.

connections: building-energy--conduction-thermal-resistance output feeds building-energy--steady-conduction-heat-rate as the alternative view heat_rate = temp_diff / resistance for the same slab, area and temperature convention.

building-energy--sensible-heat-demand and building-energy--steady-conduction-heat-rate outputs are thermal demand that can feed existing heat-to-electricity only after a seasonal-scope and unit/context alignment (instantaneous or single-event heat is not seasonal delivered_heat).
building-energy--constant-power-electricity-consumption output is purchased electrical energy that can feed existing electricity-cost only after unit (kWh) and accounting-interval context alignment.
No hydraulics link is claimed: water mass here is a declared heating mass, not a hydraulics volumetric-flow product, and no density/scope match was established.
gaps: No seasonal or empirical performance model is curated; all records are steady/constant-parameter identities or theoretical laws.
Point-instantaneous conduction rate vs time-integrated conduction energy is not separately modeled; integrate rate over a declared duration only with an explicit holding assumption.
Cooling (negative temperature change) sign conventions are excluded; heating-only nonnegative domains are declared.
Validator replays arithmetic only; physical dimensional algebra and new-domain unit conversion were checked by hand, not by the engine.
queries: A 20 W LED runs 3 h per day for 365 days at constant power. What purchased electrical energy in kWh does it consume, and what is the variable cost at a flat 0.10 USD/kWh in the same annual interval, excluding fixed charges?

How much sensible heat in joules is needed to raise 0.250 kg of water (c = 4186 J/(kg K)) from 20 C to 80 C with no phase change, and what purchased electricity does that imply through a seasonal performance model whose scope matches this single heating event?
handoff.review_notes: Arithmetic and contract checks run via the bundled validator; source fidelity, edition/locator accuracy, physical dimensions, oracle independence, assumption wording, and requires-extension classification need human review. License statements record the preface text as observed on 2026-10-31 and must be rechecked at import. No empirical or expert validation is claimed.
handoff.summary: Four requires-extension scalar relationships chaining thermal demand and constant power to purchased energy: sensible heat, steady conduction rate, single-layer conduction resistance, and constant-power electricity consumption. Seasonal audit deferred with reasons.

assumptions: Source assumption: power is delivered at a constant rate over the whole declared interval (OpenStax: E = Pt is the constant-rate special case of E = integral P dt).
Application assumption: the declared interval, device boundary and meter scope are fixed by the question; no duty cycling, standby draw or tariff change inside the interval.

constants.locator: Section 9.5 worked LED example converts watts with the factor (1 kW / 1000 W); cost subsection states 1 kW.h = 3.6e6 J, consistent with E = Pt.
constants.meaning: watts per kilowatt in the billing-energy conversion

gaps: Electrical power (W) and operating duration (h) are not in the current runtime unit set (kWh, Wh, USD, USD/kWh, 1, percent); forward execution needs power/time vocabulary and dimension support.

Context single-device:declared-interval:constant-power does not match the existing home-A annual accounting context; connection to electricity-cost needs an explicit interval-alignment change, not silent relabeling.

models.inverse_notes: Duration = energy * 1000 / power requires power > 0; power = energy * 1000 / duration requires duration > 0. Zero power with zero energy leaves duration undetermined; zero duration with zero energy leaves power undetermined. No separate inverse model is published.
limitations: Excludes variable power (use the integral form), standby/duty-cycle structure inside the interval, and fixed charges or time-varying tariffs.
Energy here is metered electrical energy for the declared interval, not seasonal delivered heat and not generic stored energy.

references.method: Independent check against the published LED example: 20 W = 0.02 kW times 3 h/day x 365 days = 1095 h gives 21.9 kW.h, matching the source's reported 21.90 kW.h. Tolerance 0.01 covers the source's two-decimal reporting.
references.provenance: Published worked result in OpenStax UP2 section 9.5 LED cost-effectiveness example (100 W vs 20 W, 3 h/day, 365 days).

references.method: Limiting identity: a device drawing no power consumes no energy over any finite duration under the constant-rate definition.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check, not an empirical observation.

rejection_cases.reason: Negative power violates the nonnegative-draw profile; export or signed-flow regimes need a different definition.

relationship.locator: Section 9.5 subsection The Cost of Electricity, unnumbered equations E = integral P dt and constant-rate E = Pt; numbered power forms Eqs. 9.12-9.13; LED worked example
relationship.original_equation: E = Pt for constant power P over time interval t (general form E = integral P dt)
relationship.translation_notes: Source states energy E in joules for SI power in watts; billing form uses kilowatts times hours. Stored variables take power in W and duration in h and output energy in kW.h, dividing by the definitional constant 1000 W/kW recorded in constants. Arithmetic literal 1000 needs no measurement source beyond the stated SI prefix, explained here and sourced to the worked conversion.

sources.evidence: Page states E = integral P dt generally and E = Pt at constant rate; defines P as the time rate of energy transfer in watts and kW.h as the billing energy unit consistent with E = Pt; LED example converts W with 1 kW/1000 W and reports 20 W over 1095 h as 21.90 kW.h.

assumptions: Source assumption: no phase change and no work done on or by the system; specific heat is treated as constant over the stated temperature interval.
Application assumption: mass, material (fixed c) and the initial/final temperature scope are declared by the question; c does not vary with temperature inside the interval.

gaps: Joules, kilograms, J/(kg K) and kelvin temperature difference are outside the current runtime unit set; forward execution needs mass/energy/temperature vocabulary and dimension support.
Output is single-event sensible heat, not seasonal delivered_heat; feeding heat-to-electricity needs an explicit seasonal-scope alignment, not relabeling.

models.inverse_notes: Mass = heat / (specific_heat * temp_rise) and temp_rise = heat / (mass * specific_heat) need nonzero denominators; zero heat with zero mass or zero rise leaves the third quantity undetermined. Cooling (negative rise) is excluded from this heating-only record and needs its own sign convention, not an algebraic flip.
limitations: Excludes phase change (latent heat), temperature-dependent specific heat, work exchange, and heat loss to surroundings during warming.
Covers heating rises only; cooling or signed temperature differences need a separate scoped record.

references.method: Independent check against the published pan-of-water example: 0.250 kg water x 4186 J/(kg C) x 60 C = 62790 J, matching the source's reported 62.8 kJ. Tolerance 100 J covers the source's three-significant-figure rounding.
references.provenance: Published worked result in OpenStax UP2 section 1.4 Required Heat example (0.250 L water, 20 C to 80 C).

references.method: Limiting identity: zero temperature change demands zero sensible heat for any finite mass and specific heat.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check, not an empirical observation.

rejection_cases.reason: Negative rise is a cooling change outside this heating-only record; the guard excludes it rather than relabeling it as negative demand.

relationship.locator: Section 1.4, Eq. 1.5; Required Heat worked example
relationship.original_equation: Q = m c delta-T for heat transfer with no phase change and no work
relationship.translation_notes: Source symbols map directly: Q to heat (J), m to mass (kg), c to specific_heat (J/(kg K)), delta-T = Tf - Ti to temp_rise (K difference). Celsius-degree differences equal kelvin differences, so the stored kelvin-difference unit needs no conversion factor.

sources.evidence: Page introduces Q = mc delta-T as the practical approximation with no phase change and no work; defines Q in joules, m as substance mass, c as specific heat in J/(kg K) or J/(kg C), delta-T as Tf - Ti; water example reports 62.8 kJ for 0.250 kg over 60 C.

assumptions: Source assumption: steady one-dimensional conduction through a uniform slab of area A and thickness d with constant conductivity and a linear temperature drop from Th to Tc.
Application assumption: faces are isothermal at the stated hot and cold temperatures over the same bounded assembly; edge effects, convection and radiation are excluded.

gaps: Watts, W/(m K), m2, m and kelvin difference are outside the current runtime unit set; forward execution needs power/length/area/temperature vocabulary and dimension support.
Output is an instantaneous loss rate, not a seasonal or cumulative heat quantity; time integration needs a separate declared holding assumption. See deferred list.

models.inverse_notes: Conductivity = heat_rate * thickness / (area * temp_diff) and temp_diff = heat_rate * thickness / (conductivity * area) need nonzero area, thickness, conductivity and difference. Thickness zero is a singularity excluded by guard; it does not model a zero-resistance contact. No separate inverse model is published.
limitations: Excludes transient warm-up, nonuniform or multilayer assemblies, temperature-dependent conductivity, and combined convection/radiation.
Heating-loss direction only (hot to cold as declared); reversed or signed flow needs its own convention.

references.method: Independent check against the published two-conductor example: the aluminum rod (k = 220, A = 7.85e-5 m2, d = 0.25 m) carrying the joint-to-cold drop 41.3 - 20 = 21.3 C reproduces the reported 1.47 W. Tolerance 0.02 covers three-significant-figure reporting.
references.provenance: Published worked result in OpenStax UP2 section 1.6 Two Conductors End to End example (joint 41.3 C, P = 1.47 W).

references.method: Limiting identity: zero temperature difference drives zero steady conduction rate for any finite geometry and conductivity.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check consistent with the source equation form.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero thickness is a singularity (division by zero) and an unmodelled contact, excluded by the positive-thickness guard.

relationship.locator: Section 1.6, Eq. 1.9; Two Conductors End to End worked example
relationship.original_equation: P = dQ/dt = k A (Th - Tc) / d for a uniform slab
relationship.translation_notes: Source rate P (W) maps to heat_rate; k to conductivity; A to area; slab thickness d to thickness; (Th - Tc) to temp_diff as a kelvin-difference quantity (C-degree differences equal K differences). Stored form equals the source equation with no added coefficients.

sources.evidence: Page gives P = dQ/dt = kA(Th - Tc)/d as Eq. 1.9 for a slab of area A and thickness d; defines P in watts, k as thermal conductivity, Th - Tc as the across-slab difference; two-rod example reports joint 41.3 C and P = 1.47 W.

assumptions: Source assumption: the same uniform-slab, steady one-dimensional geometry as the conduction rate law, so resistance depends only on thickness, conductivity and area.

Application assumption: the layer is homogeneous with constant conductivity; multilayer or composite assemblies need series/parallel composition outside this record. The two-rod source example notes its equal-area restriction.

gaps: K/W, m, W/(m K) and m2 are outside the current runtime unit set; forward execution needs thermal-resistance vocabulary and dimension support.
Area-normalized R-value (m2 K/W) and US-customary R are distinct quantities and are not this record; see deferred list.

models.inverse_notes: Thickness = resistance * conductivity * area is linear and always available within guards. Conductivity = thickness / (resistance * area) and area = thickness / (resistance * conductivity) need nonzero resistance and third quantity; zero resistance with zero thickness leaves conductivity and area undetermined. No separate inverse model is published.
limitations: Single homogeneous layer only; contact resistance, convection films and multilayer buildup are excluded.
Absolute resistance (K/W) for a declared area, not the area-normalized R-value (m2 K/W); do not interchange them.

references.method: Independent cross-check: 0.25 / (80 x 7.85e-5) = 39.81 K/W, and the published drops and rate satisfy delta-T / R = 58.7 / 39.81 = 1.47 W, reproducing the source's reported 1.47 W. Tolerance 0.2 covers rounded area and temperature reporting.
references.provenance: Geometry and reported rate from OpenStax UP2 section 1.6 Two Conductors End to End example (steel rod, joint 41.3 C, P = 1.47 W).

references.method: Limiting identity: a layer of zero thickness offers zero conductive resistance for finite conductivity and positive area.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check consistent with the source resistance form.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero area is a singularity (division by zero) excluded by the positive-area guard; the source's resistance form requires equal nonzero areas.

relationship.original_equation: R = L / k with P = A delta-T / R for joined rods (absolute form R_abs = d / (k A) so that delta-T = R_abs P)
relationship.translation_notes: Source states area-normalized R = L/k and P = A delta-T / R. Dividing by area gives the absolute slab resistance d/(kA) used here, so delta-T = resistance * heat_rate for the same slab convention. No coefficients are added.

sources.evidence: Page defines R factor as d/k, states conductive rate is inversely proportional to R, and works the two-rod example as R = L/k with P = A delta-T / R, noting the equal-area restriction.
